System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

requirements.text: The system shall detect any stationary object in the vehicle’s forward path within 2 seconds of it entering the sensor field of view using fused camera, radar, and ultrasonic data, and shall initiate an appropriate avoidance maneuver (steering, braking, or lane change) when the object’s predicted trajectory intersects the vehicle’s planned path.

The lane‑keeping algorithm shall classify lane markings with a true‑positive rate of at least 99 % and a false‑positive rate of no more than 0.5 % for non‑lane objects (e.g., barriers, guardrails) under all lighting conditions, and shall not command steering toward any object classified as non‑lane.

The collision‑threat assessment module shall compute time‑to‑collision and, when it falls below 0.5 seconds, shall command the braking system to achieve a deceleration of at least 5 m/s² within 0.2 seconds of threat detection.

If driver hands are not detected on the steering wheel for more than 2 seconds while Autopilot is engaged, the system shall issue escalating visual and audible alerts and, if hands remain absent for an additional 3 seconds, shall safely disengage Autopilot and bring the vehicle to a controlled stop.

The TACC function shall maintain a minimum safe following gap of 2 seconds using alternative sensor data (e.g., camera‑based range estimation) if the forward‑facing radar becomes unavailable, and shall generate a radar‑fault indication within 0.5 seconds of radar failure.

The driver‑monitoring subsystem shall detect driver hands on the wheel with at least 98 % accuracy and issue a hands‑off warning within 0.5 seconds of loss of detection; if the torque sensor fails, the subsystem shall switch to a secondary detection method (e.g., camera‑based hand presence) and still issue the warning.

The vehicle user interface shall display, upon each activation of Autopilot, a persistent message stating that the driver remains responsible for vehicle control and must continuously monitor the roadway, and shall require driver acknowledgement before enabling Autopilot.

The lane‑detection algorithm shall maintain lane‑keeping accuracy within ±0.3 m laterally even when lane markings have reflectivity reduced by up to 60 % of standard levels, by supplementing camera data with road‑edge or vehicle‑trajectory models.

When road‑signage or lane‑level information is unavailable or ambiguous, the system shall default to a conservative behavior: maintain the current lane, increase following distance by 20 %, and refrain from initiating lane changes until reliable perception data is obtained.

Hands‑off alerts shall be triggered only after the driver’s hands have been absent for a continuous period exceeding 1.5 seconds, and shall be suppressed if a brief glance‑away is detected via secondary cues lasting less than 0.5 seconds.
